sharedBoundaryRule.description: Loading or retrieving the Work in the context of an AI model at inference time is Execute, in all three licences' Execute definition (section 1). Placing the Work in a dataset, embedding or vector corpus, cache, or index used to develop, train, fine-tune, align, evaluate, or distil a model is Train, in the NoTrain and Reserved Train definition (section 1). Open does not need this boundary operationally because Open grants Train outright, but its Execute definition states the same rule.
sharedBoundaryRule.source: spec/SPEC.md 'Boundary rule for retrieval'; spec/licenses/*.txt section 1

generalLimitations.description: None of the three licences can restrain use of unprotectable procedure, method, or process once separated from the Work's protected expression. Each licence's Definitions (section 1) already says this ('nothing in it asserts rights over ideas, methods, or processes as such'); SPEC.md's framing ('should not silently grant permission to absorb it into a model') is a design intent, not a claim that copyright law reaches methodology.

Open's Train definition includes any 'evaluate ... distil into' without qualification. NoTrain's and Reserved's Train definition narrows the same clause to 'evaluate with a view to improve, distil into'. A benchmarking pass with no intent to improve the model reads as Train under Open's wording but arguably falls outside Train under NoTrain's and Reserved's narrower wording. Not resolved across the family in the 1.0 texts.
generalLimitations.source: legal/REVIEW_GEMINI.md finding 7; legal/COUNSEL_BRIEF.md 'Questions added 2026-09-11 (third independent AI reviewer, Gemini 3.1 Pro)'

unresolved.question: Train is defined 'to the extent that the activity requires permission from the Licensor'. If a court holds AI training on the Work to be fair use (or otherwise not requiring permission), the activity may no longer meet the Train definition, and the reservation may not bind that activity in that jurisdiction, even though the EU Article 4(3) reservation needs to stay expressed regardless of the outcome of that analysis.
unresolved.source: legal/REVIEW_GEMINI.md finding 4; legal/COUNSEL_BRIEF.md 'Questions added 2026-09-11 (third independent AI reviewer, Gemini 3.1 Pro)'

unresolved.question: Redistribution of a modification is only granted under this same licence, but the text does not define what counts as a 'modification' of a skill file. It is unclear whether an AI agent that dynamically combines this Work with a differently-licensed skill at run time produces a 'modification' subject to this condition, and whether the scope reaches skill files that embed third-party content.

The inference-only carve-out from Train reads 'provided that it is not subsequently used for Train', in the passive voice. If a third party the licensee does not control (a host, a compromised system) later uses a lawfully built inference-only index for Train, the carve-out's own wording does not say whose subsequent use matters, which could read as putting the licensee back in breach for a use it neither performed nor authorised. A proposed fix direction ('provided that You do not subsequently use it for Train') has been raised with counsel but is not adopted in the published 1.0 text.

unresolved.question: The prohibition on Executing the Work 'for the benefit of a third party' is not scoped further. Read literally, it could reach an Authorised Recipient's ordinary internal operations that merely happen to serve its own customers (for example, an MSP or consultancy diagnosing its own systems that customers rely on), which would sit uneasily against the internal-business-purposes grant in the same section. Counsel has been asked to confirm the intended breadth and whether an express carve-in mechanism (a written permission template) is advisable.

The post-termination duty to delete copies applies only 'where practicable'. For material folded into a vector index, embedding corpus, or agent memory cache, deletion of a specific item can be technically difficult, which could let a recipient argue indefinite retention is impracticable rather than merely costly. Counsel has been asked whether an objective standard would serve better than 'where practicable'.

The inference-only carve-out from Train reads 'provided that it is not subsequently used for Train', in the passive voice. If a third party the Authorised Recipient does not control later uses a lawfully built inference-only index for Train, the carve-out's own wording does not say whose subsequent use matters, which could read as putting the Authorised Recipient back in breach for a use it neither performed nor authorised. A proposed fix direction ('provided that You do not subsequently use it for Train') has been raised with counsel but is not adopted in the published 1.0 text.
